lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 25
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Way Back
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek woke before dawn to silence.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Real silence—the kind the desert had not offered since they found the staircase. No wind moved across the dunes. No night birds called. Even the donkeys stood still, ears down, as if holding their breath with him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He lay beneath his blanket and listened for the knocking. Nothing came.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Slowly he reached for the journal. The cover was colder than the desert night had any right to leave it. He opened it anyway. No new lines. The pages sat exactly as he had left them. The mark on his palm had gone cold too. For the first time since the tomb it looked like nothing more than an old scar catching the wrong light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For one treacherous second he let himself believe it was over.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he checked his father's compass. The needle no longer pointed into the earth. It pointed back toward Uruk—steady, almost eager.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not trust it. He got up anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He woke BAH-lahg first. The big man cracked one eye open.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We're leaving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg did not argue. He looked toward the staircase, said nothing, and started rolling his blanket. That silence frightened Zeek more than any argument would have.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun agreed before he finished the sentence. She had slept badly; the hollows under her eyes showed it. En-HEH-doo said nothing at all. Her silence had teeth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They broke camp in the dark and put their backs to the ridge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first few hours the desert played along. The sky went from black to bruised purple to the flat white of morning. Heat crawled up out of the sand in waves you could watch. Their shadows stretched long and blue, then shrank beneath them as the sun climbed. Zeek navigated by the old caravan markers and his father's map, the same way he always had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first marker was exactly where it should have been.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second was not.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stopped beside a half-buried stone pillar, worn smooth by centuries of wind, and traced the carved symbol with two fingers. Old work. Older than the outpost. But the direction it pointed was plain enough to read without translation.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun came up beside him.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Route marker.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Does it point toward Uruk?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It should.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She studied the stone.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Should?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the horizon, then back at the marker. It pointed east. Uruk was west. Had been west every day of his life.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg came up behind them.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Maybe we read it wrong.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek did not answer.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It happens,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Not to me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo, several paces back, smiled.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: There he is.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They kept moving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The well should have been less than an hour ahead. Zeek remembered its position the way he remembered debts: the angle of the dunes, the low ridge of black stone to the south, the broken track leading into the basin. He had marked it twice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They reached the place the map, the sun, and four separate memories agreed it should be.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: There was nothing there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Flat sand stretched unbroken to the horizon. No depression. No shadow of what had once been a well. The location itself had simply ceased to exist.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg turned in a slow circle.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We're off course.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We're not.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun had already taken sightings off the sun and the ridgeline.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The desert has stopped agreeing with itself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They found the well again when the sun stood directly overhead, throwing no shadows at all. It sat several miles off their line of travel, in a place none of them remembered crossing. The stones around its mouth were wet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stopped at the edge of the basin. Water sat inside, dark and glass-still. He could smell it from ten feet off—iron, old blood, and a taste underneath both that he did not have a word for and did not want one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg took a step toward it.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Don't,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Wasn't going to drink.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Carved fresh into the stone rim, dust still pale and scattered around the cuts, was the spiral-drop symbol. Ninsun crouched and held her fingers a hair above the grooves without touching them.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This was made recently. Hours.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nobody had carved it. They had been together every hour since leaving the ridge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down into the black water. Far below the surface—not a reflection, not a trick of light—a shape moved, and it was not still.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stepped back from the edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That was when the retreat stopped being a plan.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg wanted the staircase. Ninsun agreed with him at once.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It's the only fixed point we have left. Everything else keeps changing under us.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The staircase changed too,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It just didn't disappear.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It's more than we've got anywhere else out here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg nodded.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We go back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo did not move. She stood apart, staring at the empty shimmer of the horizon.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You keep calling it a prison because your father did,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Your father. The journal. The warnings. Every time this place scares you, you decide that means it's a trap.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Most things trying to kill us are traps.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Most things trying to kill us are honest enough to just attack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun frowned.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That makes no sense.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: It makes perfect sense.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo turned fully toward Zeek. Her eyes had gone bright—not with fear, but with something closer to hunger.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You keep assuming we need to escape from the First City. What if it isn't?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: What do you think it is, then?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She smiled the way a woman smiles when she has already picked her side.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: A kingdom.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg made a low sound in his throat. Ninsun stared at her.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You want to go back,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I want to know what's down there.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You want to walk into the place that erased an entire city from history.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo shrugged.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You say that like it wasn't impressive.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked between them. BAH-lahg wanted the staircase because walls still made sense to him. Ninsun wanted it because she needed one true thing while the world kept lying. En-HEH-doo wanted it because she had decided the First City was the biggest score of her life—bigger than money, bigger than anything she had ever put a price on.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek wanted it because his father had been there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: None of them said their real reason out loud. They turned back anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The desert did not make the return easy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They tried to pick up the caravan route that should have carried them to the ridge. Instead they found a road. The wind stripped enough dust away to show paving stones the size of coffins, fitted with a precision that made the outpost ruins look like a child's work.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun dropped to her knees at one of the joints.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This is older than the known dynasties.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: How old?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The answer seemed to cost her more than any number could have.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The road ran the wrong direction—away from Uruk, away from the ridge, toward nothing they recognized. Beside it, pressed into the sand, were footprints. Bare feet. One set. Fresh.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The prints started beside the buried road and led toward the ridge. Zeek followed them until they stopped. No second set. No drag marks. No struggle. Only a strip of faded cloth half-buried where the last footprint ended.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stopped breathing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He knew it before he touched it. The weave. The dye gone the color of old rust. The ghost of smoke and myrrh still clinging to the fibers after twelve years of desert wind that should have scoured it clean.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His father's cloak.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He picked it up. For one long moment the desert dropped away and he was eleven years old again, huddled beside a dying fire while his father draped this same cloth over his shoulders.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: Desert remembers the sun. Doesn't mean it owes you warmth after dark.
lines.note: Memory of Bel-iddin by the fire when Zik was a boy. Warm, dry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun watched him.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Is it his?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He nodded.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked toward the ridge.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then he was here.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It wanted me to think he was.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Does it matter which?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: If your father left it, he was here. If something else placed it, then what's out there knows him well enough to make you believe it. Either way, this place stopped just waiting for us a while ago.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wind moved. The footprints vanished between one blink and the next.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cloth was no longer in Zeek's hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nobody spoke. Then BAH-lahg said,
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We're going back,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: and this time no one argued.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It took until nightfall to reach the ridge. The outpost was still there. For a moment Zeek let himself believe that was good news.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he saw the staircase.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It had been twenty feet deep that morning. Now the steps dropped away into a darkness that swallowed torchlight before it traveled more than an arm's length—a darkness with weight to it, like the absence of light had learned to push back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stood at the edge.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That wasn't there.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Neither was the rest of this,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said quietly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wall at the bottom was simply gone. Only the black mouth of the stairwell remained, breathing cold up into the night air.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek pulled out the compass. The needle pointed straight down. Then, slow as a held breath, it turned and settled on the darkness of the stairwell itself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal opened on its own. Lines formed, wet ink crawling across dry paper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You tried to leave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark on his palm woke.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That was wise.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun read over his shoulder.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That's not comforting.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One final line.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You should have gone farther.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek turned to look back the way they had come.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing. Flat sand stretched unbroken in every direction. No footprints. No buried road. No proof any of them had ever stood anywhere but here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg turned a slow circle.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then how did we get back?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down into the stairwell's black throat.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I don't think we did.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From somewhere far below came three measured knocks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three more answered from the open desert behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down into the stairwell. Then he turned and looked behind them, at the empty dark where the desert simply stopped being anything at all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: There was nothing there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal turned a page on its own. A final line bled into the paper, letter by letter.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: YOU ARE ALREADY INSIDE.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The knocking began again—from everywhere at once.
